questions.question: The difference between CI and SI for 3 years at the rate of 20% per annum is Rs.160. What is the principal lent?
questions.questionHtml: The difference between CI and SI for 3 years at the rate of 20% per annum is Rs.160. What is the principal lent?
questions.solution:
Given:-

CI - SI = 160

Rate of interest(r) = 20%

Time(t) = 3 years

Formula used:-

Ci = P[(1 + r/100)t - 1]

SI = ( P × r × t)/100

Calculation:-

CI - SI = P[{(1 + 20/100)3 - 1} - {20 × 3}/100]

⇒ 160 = P[(6/5 × 6/5 × 6/5) - 1 - 6/10]

⇒ 160 = P[(2160 - 750 - 1250)/1250]

⇒ P = (160 × 1250)/160

⇒ P = 1250

Shortcut Trick Calculation:-

Difference between CI and SI for 3 years,

D = P\((\large{\frac{r}{100}})^2\).\((\large{\frac{r}{100} + 3})\)

∴ 160 = P(20/100)2.(20/100 + 3)

⇒ 160 = P(1/5 × 1/5)(16/5)

⇒ P = 160 × (125/16)

⇒ P = 1250.

questions.question: The difference between the compound interest compounded half yearly for one year and the simple interest for one year on a certain sum is Rs.200. What is the sum if the rate of interest in both the cases is 20%?
questions.questionHtml: The difference between the compound interest compounded half yearly for one year and the simple interest for one year on a certain sum is Rs.200. What is the sum if the rate of interest in both the cases is 20%?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 20000.

Given:

Difference between Compound Interest (CI) and Simple Interest (SI) for a year = Rs 200

Rate of interest = 20%

Concept:

CI (payable half-yearly) = P [(1 + r/200)² - 1]

SI for a year = P × r × t / 100

The difference between CI and SI gives the required value.

Calculation:

Let's denote the principal as P.

The CI (payable half-yearly) = P [(1 + 20/200)² - 1]

⇒ P [(1.1)² - 1]

⇒ P [1.21 - 1] = P × 0.21

The SI for a year = P × 20 × 1 / 100 = P × 0.2

The difference between CI and SI = P × 0.21 - P × 0.2 = P × 0.01

Given that the difference is Rs 200, So

P × 0.01 = 200

⇒ P = 200 / 0.01 = Rs. 20000

∴ The sum is Rs 20,000.

questions.question: On what sum of money will the difference between the simple interest and compound interest (Compounded annually) for 3 years at 5% per annum be Rs. 15.25?
questions.questionHtml: On what sum of money will the difference between the simple interest and compound interest (Compounded annually) for 3 years at 5% per annum be Rs. 15.25?
questions.solution:
Given:

Simple Interest (SI) for 3 years at 5% per annum

Compound Interest (CI) for 3 years at 5% per annum

Difference between CI and SI for 3 years = ₹15.25

Formula used:

SI = P × R × T / 100

CI = P × (1 + R/100)T - P

Difference = CI - SI

Calculation:

Let the principal amount be P.

SI for 3 years = P × 5 × 3 / 100

SI = 15P / 100

SI = 0.15P

CI for 3 years = P × (1 + 5/100)3 - P

CI = P × 1.157625 - P

CI = 1.157625P - P

CI = 0.157625P

Difference = CI - SI

⇒ 0.157625P - 0.15P = 15.25

⇒ 0.007625P = 15.25

⇒ P = 15.25 / 0.007625

⇒ P = 2000

∴ The sum of money is ₹2000.

questions.question: Find the difference between C.I and S.I for 1 year on principal of Rs.12500, if the rate of interest is 4 percent and interest is calculated according to half-yearly?
questions.questionHtml: Find the difference between C.I and S.I for 1 year on principal of Rs.12500, if the rate of interest is 4 percent and interest is calculated according to half-yearly?
questions.solution:
Given:

Principal = Rs.12500

Time = 1 year

Actual Rate = 4%

Formula:

The difference between C.I and S.I for 2 years = \(P× (\frac{R}{100})^2 \)

Where, P = principal, R = rate of interest

When Interest is calculated half-yearly, then

New Rate = R/2 

New time period = T × 2

Calculation:

According to the question,

Interest is calculated half-yearly

New Rate = 4/2 = 2%

New time period = 1 × 2 = 2 years

C.I – S.I for 2 years = \(P× (\frac{R}{100})^2\)    

⇒ \(12500× (\frac{2}{100})^2\)

⇒ \(12500× (\frac{1}{50})× (\frac{1}{50}) \)

⇒ 125/25

⇒ 5

∴ The Difference between C.I and SI for 1 year is Rs. 5

Additional InformationIf the difference between compound and simple interest is of 3 years than,

Difference = 3 × P(R)2/(100)2 + P (R/100)3

Where, P = principal, R = rate of interest

Important Points​Compound Interest means interest earned on interest.
Simple interest always occurs on only principal but compound interest also occurs on simple interest.

So, if time period is 2 years, compound interest will also apply on simple interest of first year.

questions.question: A sum of money is lent at simple interest and compound interest. The ratio between the difference of compound interest and simple interest of 3 years and 2 years is 34 : 11. What is the rate of interest per annum?
questions.questionHtml: A sum of money is lent at simple interest and compound interest. The ratio between the difference of compound interest and simple interest of 3 years and 2 years is 34 : 11. What is the rate of interest per annum?
questions.solution:
Given:

Ratio of difference in compound interest and simple interest for 3 years and 2 years = 34 : 11.

Formula used:

Difference between compound interest (C.I.) and simple interest (S.I.) for 3 years

= \(P \left(\dfrac{R}{100}\right)^2 \left(\dfrac{300 + R}{100}\right)\)

where 

P = principal

R = Rate percent per annum

Difference between compound interest and simple interest for 2 years

= \(P \left(\dfrac{R}{100}\right)^2\)

Calculation:

Let the sum be Rs. z.

Ratio of compound interest for 3 years and simple interest for 2 years

\(\dfrac{(C.I.)_3 - (S.I.)_3}{(C.I.)_2 - (S.I.)_2} = \dfrac{P \left(\dfrac{R}{100}\right)^2 \left(\dfrac{300 + R}{100}\right)}{P \left(\dfrac{R}{100}\right)^2}\)

\(\dfrac{34}{11} = \dfrac{z \left(\dfrac{R}{100}\right)^2 \left(\dfrac{300 + R}{100}\right)}{z \left(\dfrac{R}{100}\right)^2}\)

\(\dfrac{34}{11} = \left(\dfrac{300 + R}{100}\right)\)

3400 = 11 (300 +  R)

3400 = 3300 + 11R

R = 100 / 11

\(R = 9\frac{1}{{11}}\)%.

∴ Rate percent is 9(1/11)%.

questions.question: The difference between compound interest and simple interest at the same rate of interest R percent per annum on an amount of Rs. 15,000 for 2 years is Rs. 96. What is the value of R?
questions.questionHtml: The difference between compound interest and simple interest at the same rate of interest R percent per annum on an amount of Rs. 15,000 for 2 years is Rs. 96. What is the value of R?

options.text: Cannot be determined due to insufficient data
options.html: Cannot be determined due to insufficient data

questions.solution:
Given:

Principal = Rs.15000

Time = 2 years 

Difference between C.I and S.I = Rs96

Formula used:

D = P(R / 100)2 

Where,

D = Difference  

P = Principal 

R = Rate of interest 

Calculation:

According to the formula 

⇒ 96 = 15000 × (R / 100)2

⇒ 96  = 15000 × R2 / 10000

⇒ 96 = 3R2 / 2

⇒ R2 = 64 = 8% 

∴ The required rate of interest is 8%

questions.question: Aman earns a monthly interest of Rs. 400 at 10% per annum at simple interest. Sohan earns the same interest as Aman when compounded semi-annually at 10% pa. Find the difference between the amount of Aman and Sohan have with themselves.
questions.questionHtml: Aman earns a monthly interest of Rs. 400 at 10% per annum at simple interest. Sohan earns the same interest as Aman when compounded semi-annually at 10% pa. Find the difference between the amount of Aman and Sohan have with themselves.
questions.solution:
Given:

Interest earned by Aman = Rs. 400, at 10% per annum at simple interest for 1 year.

Interest earned by Sohan = Rs. 400, at 10% per annum at compound interest compounded half yearly for 1 year.

Concept used:

Compound interest = Principal(1 + Rate/100)n - Principal

Where n = time

Simple interest = (Principal × Rate × Time)/100

The effective rate of interest for 2 years at R% per annum compounded yearly = R + R + R2/100

Calculation:

 Total interest of 1 year = 12 × 400 = Rs. 4800

Simple interest = 4800 =  (principal × 10 × 1)/100

⇒ Principal of Aman = Rs. 48000

For Sohan, Compound interest = Principal(1 + 5/100)2 - Principal (Here, Rate = 5%, because rate is compounded half-yearly)

⇒ 4800 = Principal{(105/100)2 - 1}

Principal for Sohan = 4800/0.1025 = Rs.46829.26

∴ Difference between the amount of Aman and Sohan = 48000 - 46829.26 = Rs. 1170.74

Alternate MethodMonthly interest = Rs. 400

Interest for the whole year = 12 × 400 = Rs. 4800

For Aman, the rate of interest = 10%

Principal of Aman = (4800 × 100)/10 = Rs. 48000

For Sohan, the Rate of interest = 10/2 = 5% (∵ interest is compounded half-yearly)

Effective rate for Sohan = 5 + 5 + 25/100 = 10.25%

Principal for Sohan = (4800 × 100)/10.25 = Rs. 46829.26

∴ Difference between the amount of Aman and Sohan = 48000 - 46829.26 = Rs. 1170.74

questions.question: The difference between compound and simple interest on a certain sum at the rate of 8% per annum for 2 years is Rs. 470. Find the sum.
questions.questionHtml: The difference between compound and simple interest on a certain sum at the rate of 8% per annum for 2 years is Rs. 470. Find the sum.
questions.solution:
Given:

The difference between compound and simple interest = 470

Rate = 8%

Years = 2

Formula used:

Sum = difference × (100/r)n

⇒ 470 × (100/8)2 = 470 × (10000/64)

⇒ 73437.5

∴ The sum is 73437.5

questions.question: The compound interest on a sum of ₹8,400 in 3 years at a certain rate percent per annum is ₹6115.20, interest being compounded annually. What will be the difference in (₹) between compound interest on the same sum at the same rate for \(1{1 \over 2}\) years, when the interest is compounded half yearly and the simple interest on the same sum for same rate and for the same period?
questions.questionHtml: The compound interest on a sum of ₹8,400 in 3 years at a certain rate percent per annum is ₹6115.20, interest being compounded annually. What will be the difference in (₹) between compound interest on the same sum at the same rate for \(1{1 \over 2}\) years, when the interest is compounded half yearly and the simple interest on the same sum for same rate and for the same period?
questions.solution:
Given:

Principal = Rs. 8400, Time Period = 3 years

Compound Interest = Rs. 6115.20

Formula used:

Compound Interest = P × [1 + (R/100)]n - P

Simple Interest = [P × R × T]/100

Where P = Principal, R = Rate of interest, n = Time in years

Calculation:

According to the Question,

Compound Interest = P × [1 + (R/100)]n - P

⇒ 6115.20 = 8400 × (1 + R/100)3 - 8400

⇒ 6115.20 + 8400 = 8400[((100 + R)/100)3]

⇒ 14515.20/8400 = [(100 + R)/100]3

⇒ 1728/1000 =  [(100 + R)/100]3  

⇒ [(100 + R)/100] = (1728/1000)1/3

⇒ [(100 + R)/100] = 12/10

⇒ R = 20%

Compound interest for \(1{1 \over 2}\) years, when compounded half-yearly

∴ R = 20/2 = 10%, and T = 3 years

Compound Interest = P × [1 + (R/100)]n - P

⇒ 8400 × [(100 + 10%)/100]3 - 8400

⇒ 8400[(110/100)3 - 1]

⇒ 8400 × 331/1000 = 2780.4

Simple Interest on the same sum for the same rate and time,

⇒ Simple Interest = [P × R × T]/100

⇒ [8400 × 20 × (3/2)]/100 = 2520

The required difference = 2780.4 - 2520 = 260.4

∴ Hence the required difference is ₹ 260.4
